stated: Breaking the cycle of reoffending by improving rehabilitation in prisons and on release, and strengthening the supervision of offenders in the community. This includes ending prison overcrowding, recruiting more prison officers, improving training/education/work opportunities in prisons, establishing a Women’s Justice Board, replacing Young Offender Institutions with Secure Schools and Secure Children’s Homes, ensuring every prison has a ‘through the gate’ mentorship programme, introducing a National Resettlement Plan, and improving/properly funding community supervision.

source.quote: Breaking the cycle of reoffending by improving rehabilitation in prisons and on release, and strengthening the supervision of offenders in the community. Cut reoffending by: Ending prison overcrowding. Recruiting and retaining more prison officers. Improving the provision of training, education and work opportunities in prisons. Establishing a Women’s Justice Board and providing specialist training for all staff in contact with women in the criminal justice system. Replacing Young Offender Institutions with Secure Schools and Secure Children’s Homes. Ensuring that every prison has a ‘through the gate’ mentorship programme. Introducing a National Resettlement Plan to improve the rehabilitation of people leaving prison and cut reoffending. Improving and properly funding the supervision of offenders in the community, with far greater coordination between the prison service, probation service providers, the voluntary and private sectors and local authorities, achieving savings in the high costs of reoffending.

bearing_set.reason: Reducing reoffending through rehabilitation and supervision directly affects crime rates, public safety, and the functioning of the justice system.

The policy explicitly targets education, training and work opportunities inside prisons, and replaces Young Offender Institutions with Secure Schools/Secure Children's Homes — concrete mechanisms that move O7's skills and attainment indicators for incarcerated young people and adults.

Establishing a Women's Justice Board directly addresses the recognised unequal/discriminatory treatment of women in the justice system, moving the equal-treatment and minority-protection indicators for this group.

membership_note: O5 is the primary bearing (crime/justice outcomes); O7 is earned by the explicit education/skills components for prisoners and young offenders; O9 is earned specifically by the Women's Justice Board as an equal-treatment measure. No new coercive/surveillance powers are introduced so O10 is not engaged. Spending commitments are real but not specified as unfunded, and at a scale unlikely to materially move macro debt-path indicators on their own, so O12 is not included.
